claims.dataset_scale: 636,262 rows (systematic every-10th-row sample from 6.36M PaySim transactions)

claims.title: Elliptic Bitcoin AML GraphSAGE PR-AUC
claims.notes: Canonical 3-seed temporal out-of-time inductive benchmark on physical 203k-node Elliptic Bitcoin transaction graph. PyTorch GraphSAGE 2-layer mean aggregator achieves 0.3761 ± 0.0482 PR-AUC and 0.8325 ± 0.0078 ROC-AUC across seeds (42, 123, 456) under strict past-to-future temporal split (train 1-30, val 31-34, test 35-49) with validation-only checkpoint selection and validation-calibrated operating threshold.

claims.title: Credit Card Fraud Extreme Imbalance Federated Benchmark (Controlled Budget)
claims.notes: Under controlled optimization budget parity (10 dataset passes / ~35.6k optimizer steps across 3 seeds 42, 123, 456), Federated FedAvg achieves 0.8248 ± 0.0417 PR-AUC (Seed 42: 0.7788) vs Centralized 0.8219 ± 0.0364 (Seed 42: 0.7800), demonstrating empirical parity (99.83%–100.35%). Legacy unequal-budget (2 epochs) centralized baseline achieved 0.7449 ± 0.0385 (Seed 42: 0.7059).

claims.title: Differential Privacy High-Noise Utility (sigma=3.0)
claims.notes: Genuine DP-SGD (PyTorch Opacus PrivacyEngine, accountant='prv') with per-sample clipping C=1.0 and Gaussian mechanism over 20,000 synthetic transactions (15 features, 2.1% fraud prevalence, 84 test fraud cases). High-noise setting (sigma=3.0, delta=1e-5 via PRVAccountant [Gopi et al. 2021]: epsilon=0.3497) yields PR-AUC 0.3465 ± 0.1580 and ROC-AUC 0.8720 ± 0.0551 across seeds [42, 123, 456] (sample std across 3 training seeds, ddof=1), reflecting realistic utility loss (-61.35% relative to non-private ceiling 0.8965) under strict differential privacy.

claims.title: Single-Worker Localhost HTTP Benchmark Peak Throughput (Class B1 v2 - aiohttp Load Generator)
claims.dataset_scale: C=10 Concurrent Clients (3000 Requests across 3 reps)
claims.notes: Class B1 v2 Single-Worker Localhost HTTP Benchmark over local loopback TCP socket (127.0.0.1:8089/api/v1/score-transaction) served by Uvicorn (single-worker) using a separate-process aiohttp load generator under benchmark mode (rate limiting disabled to isolate pure inference capacity). Target applies strictly to successful HTTP 2xx inference transactions. Peak throughput reached 200.7 ± 23.3 successful 2xx req/s at C=10 across 3 independent repetitions (3,000 requests, 100% 2xx success, client loop lag p99=8.52ms, client CPU=0.12 cores). Following the pure-ASGI conversion of ContentTypeMiddleware, throughput improved across multiple concurrency tiers (e.g. C=10: 200.7 req/s vs 190.7 req/s; C=50: 195.4 req/s vs 170.7 req/s; C=500: 127.2 req/s vs 118.2 req/s with median latency dropping by -804ms from 4,340ms to 3,536ms). Historical HTTPX measurements (191.0 req/s at C=10, collapsing to 41.6 req/s at C=500 due to client event-loop starvation) are preserved in benchmarks/results/raw/latency_http_service_benchmark_httpx.json as VALID MEASUREMENT OF HTTPX LOCALHOST HARNESS, SUPERSEDED FOR SERVER-CAPACITY INTERPRETATION.

pre_intervention_baseline.notes: Pre-intervention synchronous FeatureStore execution on event loop yielded 89.0 req/s peak at C=10.

historical_httpx_artifact.status: VALID MEASUREMENT OF HTTPX LOCALHOST HARNESS — SUPERSEDED FOR SERVER-CAPACITY INTERPRETATION
historical_httpx_artifact.reason: HTTPX client-side event loop starvation under high concurrency suppressed client throughput to ~41-56 req/s while aiohttp achieved 118-141 req/s on the identical unchanged server.
